name: Editorial Product Gallery
summary: Each product is presented as a full-page magazine spread: a full-bleed environment photograph, a light display headline, and a small museum-label spec block — a slider that feels like turning pages of a curated design catalog rather than browsing a store.

composition: A consistent overlay grid across all slides: oversized headline pinned lower-left, spec block beneath it, filmstrip nav + counter lower-right, thin ruled dividers — the fixed frame makes product swaps feel like page turns of one publication.
Products are shot IN evocative environments (landscape, interior), never on white — each slide is a scene with the object as protagonist.
A row of small thumbnails + slide counter provides quiet navigation that never competes with the imagery.
layering: Text sits on a subtle darkening scrim over the full-bleed photo; depth comes from real photographic depth-of-field, not stacked cutouts.
The spec block reads as a museum object label: category, material, dimensions in a small ruled data block anchored under the headline.
lighting: Natural photographic light with soft atmospheric haze; a gentle bottom vignette/scrim anchors the text without hard glows.
A muted, desaturated, low-contrast grade unifies every product scene into one calm gallery mood — the grade IS the curation.
typography: Light-weight LARGE display (serif or sans) for product names against tiny tracked-out mono/sans spec labels — extreme weight and size contrast is the editorial signature.
Ruled dividers and label typography borrow from print object-catalogs.

rules: Let each environment photo dictate a muted near-monochrome duotone; the grade keeps them siblings.
Interface chrome holds ONE constant brand accent (for the buy CTA) that stays outside the photographic world.

easing: Long gentle cross-dissolves/slides with expo-out settles; nothing snaps.
Headline and spec text stagger in AFTER the background lands — imagery leads, information follows.
pacing: Slow and deliberate, ~1s+ transitions, matching the luxury register.
Each spread holds — no autoplay urgency; the visitor turns the pages.
choreography: Top-down cascade per slide: environment transitions first, then headline, then metadata block and counter update.
The eye is always steered to the product name before the specs.

gapNotes: FLUX generates environment product scenes, but the unified muted grade across a generated SET (grade-as-curation) needs the W-PHOTO color-grade/LUT pass — without it generated spreads read as unrelated stock.
Museum-label spec blocks and ruled dividers are straightforward MSDF/plane composition (no gap).
Cross-dissolve between full-bleed textured planes exists via hub transition presets.

whenToUse: Premium object brands (furniture, instruments, craft goods) with a small curated catalog.
Portfolio-of-products storytelling where perceived value matters more than conversion speed.
Briefs that supply or can generate strong environmental photography.
whenNotToUse: High-velocity e-commerce needing price, variants, and quick add-to-cart — the editorial pacing hides transactional affordances.
Large catalogs: past ~10 items the page-turn reverence collapses into slowness.
Products that photograph poorly in environments (small/flat items).

notes: Shares the reverent one-object-at-a-time register with luxury-product-microsite; they differ in stage (environment photography vs studio vitrine).

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as infinite-filmstrip-gallery and media-showreel-gallery.

exemplars.promptSummary: Single faceted crystal perfume bottle on a seamless warm-grey sweep, one soft overhead key, thin ground shadow, vast negative space — museum-label editorial minimalism.
